ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Royal Decree 30/2016 Promulgating the Law on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, as amended; Commercial Companies Law Royal Decree 18/2019; Central Bank of Oman AML/CFT Executive Regulations; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Guidelines; National Committee for Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing decisions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry of Parent Company Domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if origin state is not an Apostille Party)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners against UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List and Omani domestic notices issued under Royal Decree 30/2016. Mandatory Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) status check using credible commercial databases; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, source of wealth and source of funds verification; ongoing transaction monitoring of franchise royalty wires and local POS settlements; escalation of any hit to the Omani Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Invest Easy Portal of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) / Oman Business e-Government Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Arabic; a transliterated Latin-script version may be registered as an additional trading name. The name must include 'Single Person Company (SPC)' or its Arabic equivalent 'شركة الشخص الواحد'. Identical, phometically identical, or confusingly similar names to existing registered entities are prohibited. All Arabic names must comply with Oman's naming conventions and may not contain offensive, misleading or national-security-sensitive references.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Undersecretary of MOCIIP for Commerce within 15 business days of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the legal basis, propose alternate names, and include any evidence of identical or similar existing registrations. MOCIIP must issue a final administrative decision within 30 business days. Further recourse is available before the Administrative Court under the Law of Administrative Justice. A rejected name cannot be re-submitted unless the cause of rejection has been cured and supporting documentary evidence is attached.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are acceptable only for registered correspondence and legal-notice purposes for an SPC, provided the service provider holds a valid commercial license. For the commercial activity of franchise licensing and syrup supply for bubble tea chains, a physical local office or licensed business premises in Oman is required due to Ministry of Health, municipal food safety and franchise disclosure regulatory oversight. A purely virtual office will not satisfy substantive commercial presence requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high; estimated 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of licensing for food-beverage and franchise operations, increasing if UBO sanctions/PEP flags are present or if municipal food-safety complaints are filed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Companies Law, Royal Decree No. 18/2019, as amended, Part III on Limited Liability Companies and the implementing Single Person Company rules issued by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion; Foreign Capital Investment Law, Royal Decree No. 50/2019, Article 2 (foreign ownership).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company and Commercial Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion of the Sultanate of Oman, through the Invest Easy e-Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SPC Memorandum and Articles of Association registered with the MOCIIP Commercial Registration application, resulting in issuance of the Commercial Registration (CR) Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No fixed statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Single Person Company under Royal Decree No. 50/2019. The capital stated in the Memorandum and Articles of Association must be reasonable for the ISIC 5610 franchise and syrup supply business, fully subscribed by the sole shareholder and paid before registration. The funds are held in a blocked corporate bank account in Oman, verified by a capital deposit certificate, and released to the company's ordinary operational account after issuance of the Commercial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first formal meeting of the single shareholder of OM_SPC: 1. The declared share capital is subscribed by the sole shareholder and shall be fully paid into the corporate bank account of OM_SPC before registration; the capital deposit shall remain available after issuance of the Commercial Registration Certificate. 2. The registered office of OM_SPC is fixed at the premises specified in the lease in Muscat, Sultanate of Oman, which shall be its statutory domicile and address for legal notices. 3. The sole director and general manager of OM_SPC is appointed as authorised officer to execute all incorporation filings, open bank accounts, reserve licences and retain external advisers. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation in the Invest Easy corporate registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directorate General of Commerce and Investment, MOCIIP online portal (investeasy.gov.om)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an investor account on the Invest Easy e-Portal and select the legal form 'Single Person Company (SPC)'. Enter the proposed corporate name in Arabic and Latin transliteration and complete the reservation request using the commercial activity code 5610. Ensure the name is consistent with franchise and tea-beverage commercial descriptors and contains no restricted expressions requiring prior licence.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of sole shareholder and appointed director
Notarised power of attorney if a formation agent is engaged
Completed SPC name reservation application
Corporate and business activity declaration for ISIC 5610
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or non-compliance, submit a new reservation using an alternative Arabic/Latin transliteration or a different corporate descriptor; MOCIIP administrative appeal is available within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation and authentication of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directorate General of Notary Public and Authentication, Ministry of Justice and Legal Affairs of Oman, through a licensed Omani notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise the SPC Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic, with an English counterpart for internal control. Have the sole shareholder or their authorised agent execute the constitutional documents before an Omani notary, together with the pro-forma First Board Resolution. Where the sole shareholder is a legal entity, present apostilled or consular-legalised corporate incumbency documents and direct the notary to record the shareholding structure.
required_dossiers: Draft Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association
Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Lease contract or title deed for the intended registered office
Passport copies of shareholder and director
Foreign corporate incumbency certificate with consular legalisation or apostille, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any notarial objection by filing a signed addendum to the Articles of Association; if the Arabic translation is incomplete, provide a certified translation prepared by a licensed Oman translation office and re-submit to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocked bank account verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Omani commercial bank selected by the SPC, with MOCIIP online verification through Invest Easy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-registration corporate bank account in the name of the SPC and deposit the declared share capital. Instruct the bank to maintain the funds in a blocked account until Commercial Registration is issued. Obtain a capital deposit certificate stating the depositor, the beneficiary SPC and the amount; then link the bank certificate to the MOCIIP e-Portal so the capital is recorded as paid-up.
required_dossiers: Notarised SPC Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Signature specimen of sole director
Passport or residence card copy for banking due diligence
Source of funds declaration for the corporate account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOCIIP queries the capital deposit, request the bank to issue an updated capital verification letter and submit a corrective declaration through the portal; any AML-source query should be answered with the shareholder's bank reference and evidence of wiring instructions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration application and issuance of CR certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Directorate, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) through Invest Easy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarised SPC constitutional documents, First Board Resolution, capital deposit certificate, approved lease contract and name reservation proof to the MOCIIP Commercial Registration application. Pay the statutory registration fee online. Upon approval, MOCIIP issues the electronic Commercial Registration certificate showing the SPC legal form, registered office, board appointment and the permitted ISIC 5610 franchise and supply activities.
required_dossiers: Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Capital deposit certificate from an Omani bank
Approved lease / usufruct contract
Name reservation certificate
Payment receipt for registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to e-Portal compliance comments within the prescribed correction period by uploading the amended document; if the Commercial Registration is refused on activity-scope grounds, narrow the stated activities to franchise licensing and wholesale syrup distribution and re-file the corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry membership registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI), Muscat membership services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Commercial Registration certificate, register the SPC as an OCCI member in the same governorate as the registered office. Provide the CR certificate, constitutional documents and lease evidence, and pay the annual chamber subscription based on declared share capital and business sector. Obtain the OCCI membership certificate required for municipal licensing and expatriate employment quota approvals.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
SPC Memorandum and Articles of Association
Passport copies of shareholder and director
Lease contract or usufruct certificate
Tax registration certificate if already issued
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If OCCI requests further proof of business premises, submit a certified English translation of the lease and a copy of the CR; correct any membership classification code to align with 5610 and pay any classification difference before the chamber certificate is released.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with the General Authority for Taxation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Taxation of the Sultanate of Oman, electronic services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SPC for corporate income tax and value-added tax (VAT) purposes. If the SPC is expected to exceed the mandatory VAT registration threshold within the standard turnover assessment period, apply for VAT registration at or before the date the threshold is reached. Obtain the Tax Registration Number, and update the SPC's GJFF and business activity records to include franchise royalty income and wholesale supply of syrups.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
SPC Memorandum and Articles of Association
Lease contract
Bank details and capital deposit certificate
Passport copies of legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority sends a query about business activity, file a portal response attaching the CR and a business narrative describing the franchise, royalty collection and syrup distribution model; if VAT registration is postponed, maintain VAT register records and reapply once the threshold is met.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with the Public Authority for Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Authority for Social Insurance (PASI) of the Sultanate of Oman
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SPC as an employer with PASI following issuance of the Commercial Registration certificate and before any employment contracts are executed. Submit the SPC identification details, director personal data and projected employee headcount. This step establishes the employer file for future Omani and GCC employee social insurance contributions and also serves proof of workplace registration for labour inspection purposes.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration certificate
Director and shareholder identity documents
SPC memorandum and authorised signatories list
Lease and workplace location details
Projected staff establishment list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PASI rejects the employer file, submit a corrected authorised signatory resolution and updated CR; if the premises classification is unclear, provide the municipal lease approval showing commercial use category for 5610.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Directorate General of Commerce and Industry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion of the Sultanate of Oman, acting jointly with the Muscat Municipality Commercial and Food Safety Licensing Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial and Food Business Operating Licence for food-beverage manufacturing and wholesale syrup distribution, together with the municipal Commercial Activity Permit for franchise licensing operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Authority of the Sultanate of Oman, Directorate of Environmental Permits and Compliance
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Initial Environmental Review and Environmental Permit; not requiring a Full EIA Report unless the syrup manufacturing capacity crosses the large-industry threshold of the Environment Authority EIA schedule.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater from syrup blending, tank cleaning and food-beverage preparation must meet Omani effluent discharge standards before connection to municipal sewer: BOD5 not exceeding 25 mg/L, COD not exceeding 125 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 50 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 10 mg/L, pH within 6–9. Solvent and flavouring compound storage areas must be bunded, vapour emissions from volatile flavour compounds must be contained by closed-venting with carbon scrubbers where applicable, and hazardous cleaning waste, expired syrup and chemical containers must be manifested and disposed of through Environment Authority licensed waste contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate issued by the Royal Oman Police Civil Defence and Ambulance Department for the warehouse and blending premises; structural load inspection and building code compliance certificate from Muscat Municipality; occupational health and workplace clearance from the Ministry of Labour confirming adequate ventilation, employee welfare facilities, emergency exits and workplace signage; all clearances must be renewed with the annual Commercial Registration review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Secretariat General of Taxation (SGT), Ministry of Finance, Sultanate of Oman (formerly the Oman Tax Authority); official e-services portal: https://taxes.gov.om.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: obtain Commercial Registration (CR) from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) via the national Invest in Oman / MoCIIP e-services single window; 100% foreign ownership is permitted for a Single Person Company under the Companies Law. Step 2: apply through the SGT/OTA e-services portal (taxes.gov.om) for the unified Tax Registration Number (TRN), attaching the CR, certified MOA/AOA, registered-address proof (lease/title deed), shareholder and director identification, and required licensing documents. Step 3: complete CIT and VAT registration activation and obtain the VAT registration certificate; statutory deadlines run from commencement of commercial activity (generally within 90 days). The TRN is the single identifier used for CIT returns, VAT returns, customs declarations and employer withholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Omani-resident SPC is taxed as a juridical person on worldwide income under the Unified Income Tax Law (Royal Decree 59/2023, applicable to tax periods beginning on or after 1 January 2025); headline rate 9% on taxable income exceeding OMR 100,000 and 0% on the first OMR 100,000; special regimes apply to hydrocarbon (55%) and mining (35%) activities. No pass-through treatment is available to shareholders; 10% final withholding generally applies to dividends, interest, royalties and management fees paid by the SPC to non-residents, subject to any applicable tax treaty relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Oman does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through election. Available statutory elections and applications include: (i) tax-group election to file a consolidated CIT return with directly 100%-owned Omani subsidiaries; (ii) small-taxpayer simplification for gross revenue up to OMR 100,000; (iii) advance pricing agreement (APA) application with the OTA for the franchise royalty and syrup supply chain transfer-pricing margin; (iv) foreign tax credit election for foreign-source income; and (v) VAT elections for voluntary registration at the OMR 19,250 threshold, input-tax apportionment and tax-period selection.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Oman VAT Law (Royal Decree 121/2020) and Executive Regulations (Decision 53/2021), aligned with the GCC VAT Agreement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: annual taxable supplies exceeding OMR 38,500 (approximately USD 100,000); voluntary registration: taxable supplies exceeding OMR 19,250. Non-resident suppliers of digital or B2C services in Oman must register regardless of the local threshold, and imported B2B services are subject to reverse-charge VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Phased national e-invoicing mandate under the OTA e-invoicing framework: VAT registrants above prescribed turnover must integrate OTA-approved billing software with the OTA fiscal platform via API, submit XML/UBL invoices for near-real-time validation (clearance), and issue invoices carrying an OTA-generated QR code and digital stamp. Only cleared e-invoices support the recipient's input-VAT deduction. The roll-out is staggered by taxpayer turnover segment, with all registrants required to be on the cleared e-invoicing channel within the published OTA compliance window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for 0% VAT if they physically leave Oman within 90 days of the supply date and the supplier retains customs and transport evidence. Export of services, including franchise licensing, royalties, and syrup/IP licences supplied to an offshore franchisee, is zero-rated when the recipient is established outside Oman and the service is not connected with Omani goods or real property (place-of-supply and effective-use-and-enjoyment tests). The SPC may recover attributable input VAT and file periodic VAT refund claims for recurring excess export credits.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Oman Customs Export Declaration (Bayan single-window manifest)
Certified commercial invoice and packing list
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment to the foreign franchisee
Signed export/supply contract and, where applicable, certificate of origin
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment evidence proving receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The OTA and Oman Customs cross-match Bayan export declarations with VAT zero-rating schedules and bank remittance records. Goods failing the 90-day physical-export test are recharacterised as taxable supplies at 5% VAT, with input-VAT clawback, late-payment interest and administrative fines. Fraudulent export zero-rating, including false invoices, forged bills of lading and circular remittances, triggers penalties of up to 200% of the tax evaded, criminal prosecution or imprisonment under tax offence provisions, loss of export privileges, and commercial-registration sanctions. The OTA's clawback assessment window is generally four years, extended to ten years in cases of fraud or wilful default.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Oman (CBO) in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion for FDI-related approvals
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Omani Rial (OMR) is officially pegged to the USD at a fixed rate of 1 OMR = 2.6008 USD. Oman's exchange control regime is liberal for current account transactions, including dividend and royalty remittances, which are freely transferable after tax settlement and audited financial statements are submitted to the licensed bank. Capital account inflows and outflows, including foreign direct investment equity and shareholder loans, are permitted without prior CBO exchange-control approval for qualifying foreign-owned SPCs, provided funds arrive through licensed banks and are credited to the proper accounts with a purpose code. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal; a fully owned foreign SPC may remit net profits, branch profits, or liquidation proceeds, subject to CBO anti-money-laundering verification, submission of the annual audited accounts, tax clearance (if applicable under Oman Corporate Income Tax Law), and the absence of any commercial or administrative freeze. The rial's convertibility is effectively full for approved current transactions, but for hedging and large capital outflows counterparties are expected to transact within the USD peg corridor and via CBO-regulated swap facilities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Oman does not impose mandatory export proceeds surrender or a statutory conversion ratio on export receipts. Exporters may retain receipts in OMR or in a permitted foreign currency (commonly USD) in a CBO-licensed bank account. For the boba tea franchise supply chain, export proceeds from the sale of syrups and additives to overseas franchisees must be received via a licensed Omani bank within a commercially reasonable period (typically 180 days from shipment), supported by the underlying commercial invoice, bill of lading, and customs export declaration. There is no obligation to forcibly convert USD to OMR; however, OMR-denominated disbursements may require a spot conversion at prevailing market rates within the pegged band.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — Offshore digital electronic money institutions and non-bank EMIs cannot obtain CBO e-money licenses without a material in-country presence, and CBO regulations stipulate that payment services and e-money issuance are restricted to licensed Omani payment service providers and banks. The SPC should rely on CBO-regulated Omani banks for cross-border clearing, SWIFT, and FX. Global fintech corridors may only be used as a supplementary collection channel for low-value franchisee POS payments if the EMI has a valid CBO pass-through or is operating via a licensed Omani payment aggregator; otherwise, corporate treasury must execute all high-value royalty flows through SWIFT-enabled commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under CBO KYC rules and Oman's AML/CTF Law, at least one Ultimate Beneficial Owner and one authorized signatory with a valid Commercial Registration (CR) and SPC establishment contract should expect to complete a face-to-face or credible video-identification interview with the bank's compliance team. Remote opening is possible for low-risk corporate clients with impeccable source-of-funds documentation, but CBO examiners generally require a local director, resident manager, or a licensed corporate service provider in Oman to hold an in-person onboarding meeting at the bank's head office. Documentary wet-ink or attested signatures on board resolutions and bank mandate forms remain mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty income from a network of international franchisees with mixed beneficial-owner jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Franchise agreements, royalty schedules, due diligence files for each franchisee (UBO identification, sanction screening, licensed food-safety permits), periodic audited royalty statements, invoices and payment evidence demonstrating the commercial substance of each cross-border transaction, and a group AML policy with risk-rating methodology.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of UAE- or GCC-based intermediaries in the capital or trade chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Letters of explanation, commercial agreements showing a genuine supply-chain and distribution relationship, bank statements of the intermediary, certificates of incorporation, passport copies of UBOs, and legal and tax invoices that match the payment flow exactly.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound USD wires from multiple countries to a newly opened Omani SPC account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer Risk Assessment, source-of-funds declarations, underlying franchisee master-license and operations agreements, CPO and trade documents, historical bank statements from an existing operating entity, and a treasury policy that segregates royalty income from supply-chain disbursements to eliminate commingling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or signatory is a politically exposed person or resident of a high-risk sanctions jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP screening reports, detailed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds dossier, notarized and apostilled legal certificates, bank reference letters from prior reputable banks, and clear evidence of zero nexus to sanctioned jurisdictions or persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum capital injection (share capital and shareholder loan) routed through an intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legalized share subscription agreement, certified CR of the SPC, CBO-approved capital verification statement, board resolution approving the capital injection, overseas tax clearance certificates, entity registry extracts of the parent company, and signed SWIFT MT103 documentation with a precise purpose code.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols for the initial capital and shareholder loans must be executed via SWIFT MT103 from the parent entity's bank to the SPC's capital escrow account at a CBO-regulated Omani bank. The incoming wire must specify purpose code 'Share Capital Injection – FDI' or 'Subordinated Loan – Operational Funding' as applicable, include the SPC's Commercial Registration number and Omani bank account IBAN, and be accompanied by a signed capital contribution certificate and board resolution. CBO will automatically treat the credit as FDI; the SPC must file the capital injection with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion and the National Centre for Statistics and Information if the amount exceeds the Omani FDI threshold. The bank will perform a standard FX conversion to OMR only if the account is OMR-denominated; otherwise, USD and OMR clearing are separated. For any amount above OMR equivalent of USD 10,000,000, the bank may require a copy of the CBO or Ministry approval if the transaction falls under a restricted GATS Mode-3 category, though this franchise activity is a liberalized sector.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for syrup shipments to international franchisees and payments to third-party logistics and raw material suppliers shall be cleared via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account trade, or through irrevocable commercial Letters of Credit (LC) at sight for high-value consignments. For LC issuance, the SPC must apply to its Omani bank with the pro-forma invoice, transport documents, packing list, certificate of origin, and ISIC 5610-related franchise supply agreement. Once invoices are verified and confirmed, the negotiating bank pays the beneficiary using the clearing system of the corresponding currency (Fedwire/CHIPS for USD, SEPA/TARGET2 for EUR, or the local GCC RTGS used for OMR). All outbound disbursements must be matched against an underlying commercial invoice and export declaration, and must be covered by CBO-compliant approval for transactions above OMR 250,000 or where the purpose code indicates an overseas loan, guarantee, or security.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBO-licensed spot OMR/USD transactions at or within the pegged band (1 OMR = 2.6008 USD)
Outright forward contracts for OMR/USD with a licensed Omani bank, not requiring delivery of physical rial at maturity if underlying trade or royalty exposure is evidenced
Long-term Currency Forwards up to 12 months for franchise royalty streams from USD-denominated territories
FX Swaps (rollovers) between USD and OMR for short-term liquidity positioning without speculative intent
Cross-Currency Swaps for quarterly royalty conversion where the SPC receives USD and pays OMR-denominated franchisee royalties (structured as a deliverable swap)
Buy-Now-Sell-Later Contracts executed through licensed commercial banks for hedge accounting under IFRS 9

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Register Renewal of the Single Person Company (SPC) with renewed investment/commercial license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) – Commercial Registry via the 'Invest in Oman' online single-window platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of the original commercial registration date; filing is accepted from 30 calendar days prior to expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a monthly penalty of OMR 10 (USD 25.97) per commenced month; non-renewal for 60 days causes administrative suspension of the commercial license and may lead to strike-off from the Commercial Registry after one year of continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (including external auditor's report and owner-approval records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MoCIIP – Commercial Registry (mandatory filing of annual accounts and audit opinion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; for the standard calendar year, filing is due by 30 June; the Registrar may grant an extension upon justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory deadline exposes the SPC to fines up to OMR 500 (USD 1,298) under the Commercial Companies Law; repeated or persistent non-compliance can trigger administrative strike-off and disqualification of the responsible director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and full update of the Real Beneficiary Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MoCIIP – Commercial Registry, Real Beneficiary Register module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, coincident with the commercial register renewal; any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate ownership must additionally be notified within 15 calendar days of the occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or late filing carries penalties of OMR 100 to OMR 1,000 (USD 260–2,600) under the Oman AML/CFT Law and Beneficial Ownership Regulations; sustained non-compliance may result in suspension of the commercial license and eventual strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and supporting audited financial statements (where applicable for the SPC's assessed corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronic filing within 4 months after the end of the tax year; for a calendar-year SPC, the return is due by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of 5% of tax payable for each commenced month, capped at 25% of the tax due; inaccurate or incomplete filing attracts additional fines under Oman Income Tax Law; while tax defaults are not an automatic strike-off trigger, persistent fraudulent non-compliance may lead the Commercial Registry to suspend or strike off the entity at the OTA's request.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Every Oman Single Person Company must appoint a licensed public auditor annually; no turnover or balance-sheet exemption exists under the Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree 18/2019, as amended). The audit is mandatory irrespective of size, and the Oman Tax Authority also requires audited financial statements in support of the annual corporate income tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB and endorsed for Oman; local Omani GAAP is not a permissible substitute for statutory commercial and tax filing purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SPC must maintain a complete Real Beneficiary Register and file the UBO data with the MoCIIP Commercial Registry. Any direct or indirect shareholding transfer, change in control, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be recorded and submitted to the Registrar within 15 calendar days. The annual UBO confirmation, performed together with the commercial register renewal, legally validates the accuracy of the previous year's UBO declarations; a transfer not updated in the UBO Register is unenforceable against third parties and exposes the SPC to fines and administrative sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (owner resolutions and director/manager meetings)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic onshore tax holiday. A preferential 3% rate applies to SMEs on taxable income not exceeding OMR 100,000. Deductions are available for ordinary commercial expenses, capital allowances, irrecoverable debts, and foreign taxes under the Oman Tax Authority (OTA) rules. Free-zone tax holidays are not assumed unless the SPC is separately licensed in a designated free zone.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Electronic Income Tax Return under Royal Decree 43/2023 (legacy Form No. 1 for juridical persons) filed through the Oman Tax Authority 'Meyas' e-filing portal (https://tax.oman.om)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six (6) months from the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year SPC the return and full tax payment are due no later than 30 June of the subsequent year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial Registration (CR) number, tax card number, legal name, address, and financial year-end date of the SPC
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SPC is foreign-owned, provide the authorised tax representative's details in Oman and identify the non-resident shareholder's percentage of holding

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax per audited financial statements (P&L) prepared under IFRS as adopted by the OTA
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Omani SPC's audited financial statements; consolidated group returns are not permitted for this SPC

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Addbacks and deductions: disallowed entertainment, unpaid provisions, excessive head-office charges, and statutory capital allowances claimed instead of book depreciation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharging of foreign parent or affiliated expenses is deductible only with supporting contracts and arm's-length transfer pricing evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses (up to five tax years) set off against current-year taxable income, subject to continuity-of-trade and ownership rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the Omani SPC cannot be transferred, surrendered, or offset at the foreign shareholder level

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all controlled transactions with foreign franchise master licensors, syrup suppliers, sub-licensees, and financing providers, including the transfer pricing methodology applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory schedule when aggregate controlled transactions exceed OMR 1,000,000; omission invites a fixed penalty and elevated audit threat

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax at 15% (or 3% for qualifying SME tranches), net of withholding tax credits on Omani-sourced income and any eligible foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign shareholders carry on no activity that creates a permanent establishment in Oman, no further Omani corporate liability attaches to them beyond the statutory dividends withholding tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: OMR 100–500 fine plus OMR 10 per day of delay, capped at OMR 1,000; late tax payment attracts a monthly surcharge of 1% of the unpaid tax, accruing continuously; failure to file exposes the SPC to discretionary assessment by the OTA and inclusion in the public tax-defaulters register.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed to a non-resident shareholder, imposed under Royal Decree 43/2023; under the prior law dividends were generally outside the scope of Omani withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction for the relevant fiscal year; (2) provide the Omani SPC as withholding agent with a beneficial-ownership declaration supported by the TRC; (3) ensure the SPC retains the declaration and applies the reduced rate at the time of remittance; where the OTA requests pre-confirmation, the SPC must obtain a letter of treaty-relief approval before repatriation. If the relief is rejected or the documentation is deficient, the SPC is liable for the shortfall, penalties, and monthly surcharges.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 10% statutory withholding tax for franchise royalties, IP licence fees, and debt interest paid to non-residents without a permanent establishment in Oman; treaties typically reduce interest to 0%–10% and royalties to 8%–10%; in the franchise model, royalty lines must be separated from syrup-supply sale-of-goods transactions, which are not subject to withholding tax when properly structured as trading flows.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: OMR 1,000,000 - aggregate annual controlled transactions triggering the mandatory preparation and filing/support of Local File and Master File with the Oman Tax Authority, in accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Oman's Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) cover enumerated activities such as banking, insurance, fund management, shipping, finance/leasing, and holding-company activities; boba tea franchise licensing and syrup supply are not listed ESR activities. However, the OTA's General Anti-Abuse Rules and DTA limitation-of-benefits clauses require the SPC to demonstrate real premises, qualified staff, board decision-making in Oman, and genuine commercial risk for its royalty income. A shell SPC with no substance risks treaty denial, GAAR recharacterization, and penalty exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting franchise royalty income or daily cash/POS receipts from tea outlets, issuing false supplier invoices, destroying accounting records, or making fraudulent adjustments to taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of underpaid tax plus 1% monthly late-payment surcharge; evasion fines of OMR 5,000–10,000 or up to 200% of the evaded tax in aggravated OTA determinations; imprisonment of 6 months to 3 years for responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who approved false returns assume joint and several civil liability for the evaded tax; courts may impose travel bans, passport surrender, disqualification as manager, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Substance Abatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a foreign-owned SPC with no physical office, no active employees, and no business plan while booking large franchise royalty and commission income out of Oman through a zero-substance conduit to avoid the 15% Omani tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR denial of conduit status: income is re-attributed to the Omani SPC, controlled-transaction deductions are disallowed, and an administrative penalty of up to 100% of the additional tax assessment is imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who stripped or dissipated corporate assets to frustrate the assessment are personally liable for the SPC's unpaid tax under the piercing-the-corporate-veil doctrine; travel bans and asset-freezing orders are routinely issued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold the 10% Omani WHT on royalty, interest, or dividend remittances to a non-resident licensor or parent, or applying a treaty-reduced rate without a valid TRC and beneficial-ownership filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SPC as withholding agent is liable for the unpaid WHT, penalties of 100% of the amount not withheld, monthly late-payment surcharge, and potential criminal prosecution for misuse of treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally accountable for WHT debts under the Oman Companies Law joint-liability provision; courts may issue individual travel bans until the WHT and related damages are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Anti-Money-Laundering Breach via Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring daily cash and POS settlements through multiple nominee bank accounts, splitting transactions to stay below Omani reporting thresholds, or routing franchise royalty wires through sanctioned or opaque intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under Oman's AML Law (Royal Decree 30/2016 as amended): fines up to OMR 50,000, confiscation of assets, freezing orders, imprisonment up to 10 years for money-laundering offences, and revocation of the commercial licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are criminally liable for failing to file STRs/SARs with the Oman Financial Intelligence Unit; personal assets, pensions, and board positions are subject to confiscation and automatic travel bans.
